newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - WASHINGTON POST FRONT PAGE - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - WASHINGTON POST FRONT PAGE - AUG 13.

text.p: The Washington Post included the following stories on its front page on Aug. 13:
WASHINGTON - The Clinton administration released figures showing public assistance rolls continue to decline sharply with the percentage of people on welfare at its lowest level since 1970.
BROOKLYN, NEW YORK - New York City requires its welfare recipients to work off their monthly checks by sweeping streets, cleaning parks and doing other municipal chores.
RICHMOND, VIRGINIA - Former Virginia gov. Douglas Wilder is injecting himself into the 1997 race for governor by accusing his fellow Democrat Donald Beyer of pandering to African-American voters.
ANAHEIM, CALIFORNIA - There is a growing sentiment among major baseball team owners for a sweeping realignment in the sport.
WASHINGTON - The Clinton administration intends to greatly expand the number of white women enterpeneurs eligible for the federal program that aids minority businesses.
MEXICO CITY - U.S. and Mexican officials are trying hard to demonstrate their zeal in fighting drug traffickers.
